$comment: R1728 — the analysis tool's navigation, written down once, in neutral
vocabulary, as the behaviour reference draws it.
WHY THIS IS A FILE AND NOT A RUST CONSTANT. The application's rail is a
Rust table (`spec::RAIL`) because a seat needs facts a specification does
not fix: its icon, its page, the wording of its refusal. If the
specification lived beside it, written by the same hand in the same edit,
a conformance test would be asking the thing under test for the answer.
It is a separate artifact, reviewed as a claim about the reference rather
than as code.
EXTRACTION. The reference is not in this repository and must not be. The
procedure is thirty seconds and is recorded in the session memory note on
the behaviour reference: the three delivered screens each draw the same
rail, so pulling the seat list off any one of them and checking the other
two agree is the whole of it. Measured 2026-08-19: eight seats, identical
order on all three screens, and the only difference between the screens is
which seat is marked current.
R1946 — THERE ARE TWO REFERENCES AND THIS FILE COULD NOT SAY WHICH IT
MEANT. The sentence at the top said `as the behaviour reference draws it`
and the extraction note beside it said `the three delivered screens`, and
those are two different artifacts: the SCOPE reference is the first-stage
screen mockup, and the BEHAVIOUR reference is the working prototype, which
is a superset of it. Every fact in `canon` came from the scope one. Two
seats disagree between them, and the disagreement is the whole of what a
person saw missing when they opened the window on 2026-09-01.
Measured that day, at the command, on both files. The scope mockup draws
`Topology` and `Sessions` LOCKED, each naming the later-stage requirement
that books it — that is where `standing: closed` below comes from and it
is still true of that file. The behaviour prototype BUILDS both: its rail
moves to either seat like any other, the section-selected predicate exists
for both, and each has a full view of its own. Its rail has eight seats and
NOT ONE of them is locked.
So each seat now carries TWO standings, because one field could only ever
answer for one reference, and a reader had no way to tell which. `standing`
is the scope mockup's and gates the first-stage reproduction, which is
complete. `behaviour` is the working prototype's and is what the
second-stage work is measured against. `second_phase_owed` below is the
derived difference: a seat this build closes that the behaviour reference
builds. It is the list that was invisible while there was one field.
VOCABULARY. The reference's product, protocol and resource words are
replaced by the words the tool class uses generally. Structure and
behaviour are what is being reproduced; the wording is not.
THE TWO HALVES. `canon` is what the reference does. `owed` is where this
build does not do it yet, each entry carrying why. The gate asserts the
difference between the built rail and `canon` is EXACTLY `owed` — so a new
divergence fails, and so does an owed one that has been paid off without
this file being told. The second direction is the one that keeps the
number honest.

$second_phase_comment: R1946 — WHERE THIS BUILD IS BEHIND THE BEHAVIOUR REFERENCE, as opposed to
behind the scope mockup, which `owed` answers and which is empty.
An entry here is a seat whose `behaviour` is `built` and which this
application still closes. The gate derives that set from the rail and this
file and asserts it EQUALS the keys listed here — so a seat that quietly
stops being reproduced fails, and so does one that gets built without this
list being told. Same ratchet as `owed`, over the other reference.
⚠ These are NOT first-stage reproduction gaps. The scope mockup locks both
seats and this build locks them the same way, naming the same requirement,
so the first stage is reproduced. They are the second stage, which the
owner named on 2026-08-19: reproduce the first stage, then improve past it.
A person asked for exactly these two on 2026-09-01.
CAN THIS REACH ZERO? Yes, and that is the only way it may: by building the
sections. Nothing else in the tree removes an entry — the derivation reads
the live rail, so an entry deleted here without the section being built
fails the gate on the next run.
NOT THE SAME LIST AS `docs/analyzer-reserved-spec.json`'s `built`, and the
two are named here so neither is mistaken for the other. That one records
a seat the SCOPE mockup locks and THIS BUILD has since built — the second
stage arriving early, us ahead. This one records a seat the BEHAVIOUR
reference builds and this build still closes — us behind. Dual directions
of one axis, and R1946 found only this one was ever written down.
⚠ That file's `deferred` register carries the same conflation this one had
until R1946: it says `as the behaviour reference states it` while every
fact in it is the scope mockup's. Its subject is which requirement books
which capability, which the mockup is the right source for, so nothing in
it is wrong — but the sentence naming its source is, and no gate here

$owed_comment: `sentence` is the divergence VERBATIM, as the framework renders it. That
is deliberate and it is the ratchet: any change to the built rail, and any
change to how a divergence is worded, makes the gate fail until somebody
reads this file and decides what the new sentence should be. A looser
match — the key alone, or a substring — would let a seat drift from
`elsewhere` to `unbuilt`, or from renamed to absent, without a word.
$paid_comment: R1729 paid off `packets`. Its entry said the fix was a mount rather than a
build, and it was: the capture viewer's package gained a `[lib]`, its
binding gained a `pub`, and the shell mounted it. Not one line of the
screen changed.
R1730 paid off `keys`, and that one was a BUILD: the section did not exist
in this tree in any form. `hello-key-patterns` is it — a section header
with a derived summary and a live filter, a seven-column declaration list,
and a record pane of eleven parts whose last is the reference's own action
out of the section, drawn and refused with the reason THIS file gives the
seat it leads to. Its own surfaces are checked the same way this rail is,
against `docs/analyzer-keys-spec.json`.
R1731 paid off `logs`, and with it the list is EMPTY: every section the
reference opens, this build opens. `hello-log-view` is it — a header
carrying a capture mark, a live filter and an exclusive severity choice; a
five-column event list; and a decode pane whose last part is the frame's
own bytes, drawn through the framework's byte-dump geometry. Its three
surfaces are checked the same way this rail is, against
docs/analyzer-logs-spec.json.
★ The application's `Seat::Unbuilt` arm went with it. Nothing constructs
it any more and an unconstructed variant is a dead_code error under this
workspace's lints, so the compiler is what reported the rail can no longer
SPELL 'specified and not built'. The framework's
`UnavailableKind::Unbuilt` is untouched and still has consumers — the
vocabulary is the framework's, and any product built against a written
specification passes through that state.
An entry is DELETED rather than marked done, because the gate asserts the
live difference EQUALS this list. A paid divergence left here would fail
just as loudly as a new one — which is the point: the list cannot quietly
describe a worse build than the one that exists. An EMPTY list is the
strongest form of that: there is nothing left to describe.
